title_as_printed: Measurements of the Density, Speed of Sound, Viscosity, and Derived Thermodynamic Properties of Geothermal Fluids
experimental_method: Anton Paar DMA4500 densimeter, SVM3000 Stabinger viscodensimeter and DSA 5000M sound-speed analyser at atmospheric pressure, 277-343 K, on four natural geothermal brines of Dagestan.
uncertainties_stated: Table 3 footnote: DMA4500 u(T)=0.01 K, u(rho)=0.00025%; SVM3000 u(T)=0.005 K, u(rho)=0.01%, u(eta)=0.17%; DSA 5000M u(rho)=0.005%, u(c)=0.05% (95% level). Abstract: combined expanded uncertainty rho 0.0005% (DMA), 0.02% (SVM), 0.01% (DSA); eta 0.35%; c 0.1%.
quality_remarks: Natural multicomponent brines (salinity 0.9-6.3 g/L, mostly Na-Cl/SO4); not binary NaCl/KCl/CaCl2 solutions, so composition is only approximate for the six-ion set. Samples contain dissolved N2/CO2/CH4; authors report gas release above 343 K, so measurements stop at 343 K. Densities from the three instruments differ by up to ~1 kg/m3 (e.g. No. 4 at 333.15 K: 982.90 SVM vs 983.80 DSA). Source year: journal volume 61 (2016); DOI number 2015 in the key. Supporting Information noted but not needed.
